svg.title: A Halloween evening that welcomes everyone

text.tspan: Everyday English - C1 - 2026/10/27 - 01 - Essay
A costume creates a playful Halloween character.
Pexels · 29225548
A Halloween evening that welcomes everyone
The decision to prepare a Halloween evening may appear ordinary, yet it exposes a recurring tension between arrangements that make life manageable
and experiences that resist being prescribed. A defensible approach combines proportionate preparation with a willingness to reconsider whose interests a
plan serves.
Preparation has value because planning the route and the costumes helps everyone stay comfortable. In the present case, we check that costumes allow
clear vision and choose a well-lit route. Such an intervention is modest, but that modesty is its strength: it removes a foreseeable obstacle without claiming
to determine the entire experience. Structure is useful to the extent that it releases attention rather than consuming it.
That argument requires a qualification, however: clear choices make sharing treats more considerate. For instance, we keep ingredient information
available and offer a non-food option. An arrangement that appears efficient from one standpoint may impose costs elsewhere. Listening to those affected
is therefore not an optional gesture of goodwill; it supplies information without which the plan cannot be adequately evaluated.
The resulting principle is one of proportion. Preparation deserves support when it clarifies responsibilities and protects time, while responsiveness
prevents it from hardening into an end in itself. To judge the experience well is to examine both what the arrangement enables and what it may
inadvertently exclude.
BUILD YOUR OWN · State a focused main idea. Develop one supporting reason in each body paragraph, with a concrete example. Conclude by
connecting the two reasons without introducing a new argument. Use the structure as a model; write about an experience of your own.
Explain the meaning before looking at the model answer. What two reasons support the main idea? Explain one example. (Model: The two reasons are
that planning the route and the costumes helps everyone stay comfortable and that clear choices make sharing treats more considerate. One example is
that we check that costumes allow clear vision and choose a well-lit route.)
